source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Accept the request because discharge ends the professional relationship and therefore removes boundary concerns.","B":"Accept the request if the former patient initiated it, because initiation transfers responsibility for the boundary.","C":"Maintain the professional boundary and decline personal online social contact, following employer and board guidance.","D":"Decline the friend request but offer a personal phone number instead because private texting is outside boundary rules."}}
source_row.rationale: NCSBN advises maintaining professional boundaries in electronic media and using caution with online social contact with patients and former patients. A patient initiating contact does not automatically make a personal relationship appropriate. The safest response is to preserve the professional boundary and follow employer and board-of-nursing guidance.
source_row.source_detail: NCSBN — Professional Boundaries / Social Media: maintain professional boundaries in electronic communication and use caution with current/former patient social relationships; patient initiation does not remove boundary risk. source_row.stem: After discharge, a former patient sends the nurse a friend request on a personal social-media account. Which response best aligns with professional-boundary guidance?
